'''Desi Justice Carton''' (born August 5, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Laketown Squadron]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]].

==Early life==
Growing up, Carton's family moved several times before settling in [[Geneseo, Illinois]]. While living in Geneseo he attended St. Malachy Catholic School, and also went to the Geneseo Middle School. He excelled at baseball and could throw 75 miles an hour by seventh grade. He also played running back on the football team, but a rotator cuff injury forced him to concentrate on basketball. Carton moved to [[Bettendorf, Iowa]] after eighth grade and he attended [[Bettendorf High School]], where he became a starter on the basketball team as a sophomore.<ref name="Coss">{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Coss|title=Bulldogs' Carton makes meteoric rise to stardom|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/bulldogs-carton-makes-meteoric-rise-to-stardom/article_7899f7cc-0622-578a-838a-eddbab14f977.html|work=[[Quad City Times]]|date=December 1, 2018|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, he was a first-team all-state pick, averaging a school-record 26.3 points per game to go with 5.7 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game. He scored 49 points against [[Davenport West High School]] during his senior season. Carton led the Bulldogs to a 21–2 season and the top of the Class 4A state rankings before they fell to [[Dubuque Senior High School]] in the state Sweet 16 despite 27 points from Carton.<ref name="helwagen">{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Helwagen|title=A Class By Itself: Holtmann has high hopes for 2019 signee haul|url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/LongFormArticle/Ohio-State-Buckeyes-mens-basketball-recruiting-class-judged-Big-Tens-best-for-2019-131467527/#131467527_1|work=247 Sports|date=April 24, 2019|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Carton averaged 24.4 points, 7.6 rebounds and 6.0 assists per game.<ref name="doxsie">{{cite news|first=Don|last=Doxsie|title=Bettendorf's Carton leaving Ohio State program|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/college/basketball/bettendorf-s-carton-leaving-ohio-state-program/article_b3186d75-a60d-571d-bf1c-61bc343b1174.html|work=[[Quad City Times]]|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> Carton finished his career as the all-time leading scorer with 1,198 points and was among the school's all-time leaders in rebounds (372) and assists (257).<ref>{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Coss|title=Carton, Hilmer share Mr. Basketball honor|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/carton-hilmer-share-mr-basketball-honor/article_7a7f5873-415e-5741-8f47-751c137ff030.html|work=[[Quad City Times]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> He was named Co-[[Iowa Mr. Basketball]] in 2019, alongside Jake Hilmer. In AAU play, Carton competed for the Iowa Barnstormers before joining the Quad City Elite.<ref name="cowinner">{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Jeff |date=March 12, 2019 |title=Iowa all-state boys' basketball 2019: Jake Hilmer, DJ Carton named Mr. Basketball co-winners |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowa-prep-sports/basketball/iowa-high-school-all-state-basketball-teams-2019-mr-basketball-hilmer-carton-20190312 |access-date=April 22, 2020 |work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]}}</ref>

Ranked the 34th best player in his class and a four-star recruit, Carton committed to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] on July 14, 2018, over offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], among others.<ref>{{cite news|first=Bill|last=Landis|title=5-star point guard DJ Carton commits to Ohio State basketball: What it means for the Buckeyes|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2018/07/5-star_point_guard_dj_carton_c.html|work=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=July 14, 2018|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Carton was named the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] preseason freshman of the year, but [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] transfer [[CJ Walker (basketball)|CJ Walker]] started ahead of him at point guard to begin the season.<ref name="doxsie" /> Carton scored a season-high 19 points on December 15, 2019, in a 84–71 loss to [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Minnesota knocks off No. 3 Ohio State 84–71|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166118|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 15, 2019|access-date=April 22, 2020}}</ref> On January 26, 2020, Carton scored 17 points and had three assists in a win over [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]]. He decided to take a leave of absence from the team on January 30, citing mental health issues.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Ohio State's D.J. Carton takes leave, cites mental health|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28602887/ohio-state-dj-carton-takes-leave-cites-mental-health|work=[[ESPN]]|date=January 30, 2020|access-date=April 2, 2020}}</ref> Carton averaged 10.4 points and 3.0 assists per game as a freshman, shooting 40% from 3-point range. Following the season, he opted to transfer from Ohio State.<ref>{{cite news|first=Kyle|last=Boone|title=Ohio State freshman D.J. Carton enters transfer portal after stepping away for mental health reasons|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ohio-state-freshman-d-j-carton-enters-transfer-portal-after-stepping-away-for-mental-health-reasons/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 19, 2020|access-date=April 2, 2020}}</ref>

On April 15, 2020, Carton committed to continue his career at [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Evan|last=Daniels|title=OSU transfer DJ Carton commits to Marquette|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/DJ-Carton-Basketball-Marquette-Transfer-OSU-146103315/|website=247Sports.com|publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|date=April 15, 2020|access-date=April 15, 2020}}</ref> He was granted immediate eligibility by the NCAA.<ref>{{cite web|first=Stephen|last=Means|title=Former Ohio State basketball player D.J. Carton granted immediate eligibility at Marquette after transfer|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2020/06/former-ohio-state-basketball-player-dj-carton-granted-immediate-eligibility-at-marquette.html|work=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=June 17, 2020|access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> Carton averaged 13 points, 4.1 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. After the season, he announced he was entering the [[2021 NBA draft]] and hiring an agent.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=D.J. Carton won't return for another season at Marquette, but will enter NBA draft and hire agent|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/04/28/d-j-carton-turning-pro-after-one-season-marquette-and-ohio-state/4881802001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]|date=April 28, 2021|access-date=June 22, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Greensboro Swarm (2021–2022)===
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Carton signed a contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on August 7, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign DJ Carton|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-dj-carton|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 8.<ref>{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive DJ Carton and Xavier Sneed|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-waive-dj-carton-and-xavier-sneed|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}}</ref> On October 24, he signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Trujillo|title=Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster And Coaching Staff For 2021-22|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarmannouncetrainingcamproster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}}</ref>

===Iowa Wolves (2022–2024)===
On November 2, 2022, Carton was named to the opening night roster for the [[Iowa Wolves]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Iowa Wolves Finalize Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-finalize-opening-night-roster/n-5895237|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=November 2, 2022}}</ref>

On October 19, 2023, Carton signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign D.J. Carton|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-d-j-carton|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref> but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref> On October 29, he returned to Iowa.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors / Raptors 905 (2024)===
On February 21, 2024, Carton signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]]<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN CARTON TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-carton-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2024|access-date=February 21, 2024}}</ref> and on March 2, he signed a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN CARTON TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-carton-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref> On December 10, he was waived by the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE CARTON|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-carton|website=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2024|access-date=December 10, 2024}}</ref>

===San Diego Clippers (2025)===
On January 29, 2025, Carton joined the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=San Diego Clippers Acquire D.J. Carton from Iowa Wolves|url=https://sandiego.gleague.nba.com/news/san-diego-clippers-acquire-d-j-carton-from-iowa-wolves|website=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2025|access-date=January 29, 2025}}</ref> In 19 games with the Clippers, Carton averaged 13.1 points and 4.9 assists per game.<ref name="birmingham">{{cite web |title=Birmingham Acquires Returning Player Rights To D.J. Carton |url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-acquires-returning-player-rights-to-d-j-carton |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 20, 2025 |date=August 21, 2025}}</ref>

===Birmingham Squadron (2025–present)===
On August 21, 2025, Carton was acquired by the [[Birmingham Squadron]] in a four-team trade.<ref name="birmingham" />

==Personal life==
Carton was born in [[Pineville, North Carolina]]. Carton's mother Jennifer played volleyball at the [[University of Colorado]]. His father [[Desi Wilson]] played basketball and baseball at [[Fairleigh Dickinson University]] before being selected in the [[1991 Major League Baseball draft]] by the [[Texas Rangers (baseball)|Texas Rangers]] and enjoying a short career with the [[San Francisco Giants]]. His maternal grandfather Gene Meeker played basketball at the [[University of Iowa]] during the 1950s. Carton has not seen his father since the age of four. When his mother married Dale Carton, he changed his name from Desi Junior Wilson to Desi Justice Carton.<ref name="Coss" />
